sites.residue_label: stalk between EC6 and TM helix
sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Anti-Myc antibody staining of non-permeabilized cells confirmed surface display: staining was observed at the cell periphery and cell-cell junctions in transfected cells, indicating intact trafficking and surface localization of the tagged full-length protein.
sites.rationale: All three ledger lines (L1–L3) from PMC12157453 describe a Myc tag inserted in the extracellular stalk between EC6 and the TM helix of cPCDH constructs; the directly validated protein is γC3 (PCDHG-C3), making PCDHB3 an indirect/ortholog case. PCDHB3 is a beta-clustered protocadherin sharing the identical six-EC-domain + stalk + TM + ICD architecture, so the stalk region (approximately residues 630–689, fully extracellular per landmarks) is the homologous insertion site. No specific residue is named in any ledger line, so insert_after_residue is null and the site is region-level. The stalk is well clear of the TM boundary (TM starts at 690), satisfying the ≥3-residue rule. PMC12157453 reports full-length cPCDH constructs (validated on γC3/PCDHG-C3) carrying a Myc epitope tag in the extracellular stalk between EC6 and the TM helix, co-expressed with an intracellular fluorescent protein; surface display was assessed by anti-Myc antibody staining of non-permeabilized transfected cells.

sources.claim: For derived constructs including the myc tag, the tag was positioned in the stalk region between EC6 and the transmembrane helix ( Figure S1A ), equivalently to previously validated constructs ( 21 ).

literature_notes: All three ledger lines derive from a single paper (PMC12157453) and describe the same experimental approach: a Myc tag in the extracellular stalk between EC6 and the TM helix of clustered protocadherin (cPCDH) constructs. The directly validated protein is γC3 (PCDHG-C3, a gamma-protocadherin); PCDHB3 is a beta-protocadherin and a close ortholog sharing the same domain architecture. No specific residue number is given in any ledger line, so the site is region-level only (insert_after_residue = null). No ledger line supports an N-terminal extracellular tag or any other extracellular loop insertion for PCDHB3 or its close orthologs. The C-terminus (residues 712–796) is intracellular and therefore not a surface-tag candidate. No abrogating insertions or intracellular insertions are reported in the ledger for this protein.
